items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Now whose on the date? Teddy Wilson and his orchestra. But look who's on the date? ... Danny Barker on bass. Milt Hinton, Cozy Cole, and Billie Holiday.

ctx.x: the thing, on the strength of the recommendation that Jo and Cozy, as being a pretty good guy in the bass section, they would use me. Now if Basie was in town they would use Jo Jones and Walter Page. If John Kirby's band happened to be in town at that time, and John Kirby certainly had seniority over me at that particular time, then John Kirby would be the bass player. So this is why the discography reads with all these different guys.

Because you remember, Bill, since you're here, you were stationary. Milt had a position because after he left from Cab they were booked for a year and H! Six months in New York and six on the road. they had gone and entered a different category. A Now I have to jump from '37 to come to 1939, January 30. Now whose on the date? Teddy Wilson and his orchestra. But look who's on the date? Roy Eldridge, Bennie Carter. Bennie had just come back from Europe. Ernie Powell. Teddy Wilson on piano. Danny Barker on bass.…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He came up with that smooth thing which Jo Jones and them did with Basie.

ctx.x: I’m with Lucky Millinder for three years. We played everything between Duke and Cab. What they didn’t want, they shove in Lucky Millinder. Irving Mills was handling Lucky Millinder for a while. Lucky Millinder mess up with the money. Drank it. Throwed it away in the salary. They got mad with him. Said, “We got to get rid of this monkey.” So he never was a success no more, because you couldn’t trust him to bring the salary back in. That was the end of . . . So I’m with Lucky Millinder’s band. Lucky

Millinder’s hitting from here. Going, playing one-nighters here. Going to play a theater there and three or four one-nighters. He’s hitting and missing. He’s walking around all begging poor, but he done lost favor with the big dogs, the people who controlled everything. They said he’s . . . you can’t depend on him. I guess Lucky didn’t like it, people taking a big slice of his money. Some people just can’t stand that, but that’s a part of the game. Them people got to keep their offices going.
